paragraphs.title: Entering the Land and Bringing the Firstfruits

easy.question: What is a person commanded to take from the land?
answers: The first of every fruit
Stones from the field
Silver vessels
easy.explanation: The verse commands the person to take the first of the fruit of the land.

easy.question: Where does the person go with the basket?
answers: To his home
To the place the Lord will choose
To the city gate
easy.explanation: The person goes to the place where the Lord will choose to place His name.

easy.question: Who takes the basket from the person’s hand?
answers: The king
The head of the family
The priest
easy.explanation: Verse 4 says that the priest takes the basket from the person’s hand.

medium.question: What is the correct order of the actions described in these verses?
answers: Take fruit, put it in a basket, and go to the chosen place
Go to the chosen place, take fruit, and settle in the land
Give it to the priest, pick fruit, and enter the land
medium.explanation: First the person takes the first of the fruit, then puts it in a basket, and finally goes to the place the Lord will choose.

medium.question: What does the phrase “put it in a basket” show about the basket?
answers: It is an altar
It is a container for carrying the fruit
It is a field
medium.explanation: The context shows that the fruit is placed in a container and carried to the priest.

medium.question: Why does the person say that he has come to the land?
answers: Because he bought it with his money
Because he found the first fruit there
Because the Lord swore to give it to Israel’s fathers
medium.explanation: The person declares that he has come to the land the Lord swore to give to the fathers.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the phrase “the first of all the fruit of the earth”?
answers: The first and best fruits should be brought
Only fruit that fell to the ground should be brought
The entire harvest should be brought at once
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to the first fruits, not to the entire harvest or to fruit that has fallen.

challenge.question: What does the priest do after the person comes to him and speaks?
answers: He eats the fruit immediately
He takes the basket and sets it before the altar
He returns the basket to the person’s house
challenge.explanation: Verse 4 says that the priest takes the basket and sets it before the altar of the Lord.

challenge.question: What is the connection between Israel’s settling in the land and bringing the firstfruits?
answers: Firstfruits are brought before entering the land
Firstfruits are brought only after leaving the land
Firstfruits are brought after the people enter, possess, and settle in the land
challenge.explanation: The command is described after entering, possessing, and settling in the land the Lord gave them.

questions.question: What can be understood from the phrase “the first of all the fruit of the earth”?
answers: The first and best fruits should be brought
Only fruit that fell to the ground should be brought
The entire harvest should be brought at once
questions.explanation: The phrase refers to the first fruits, not to the entire harvest or to fruit that has fallen.

questions.question: What does the priest do after the person comes to him and speaks?
answers: He eats the fruit immediately
He takes the basket and sets it before the altar
He returns the basket to the person’s house
questions.explanation: Verse 4 says that the priest takes the basket and sets it before the altar of the Lord.

questions.question: What is the connection between Israel’s settling in the land and bringing the firstfruits?
answers: Firstfruits are brought before entering the land
Firstfruits are brought only after leaving the land
Firstfruits are brought after the people enter, possess, and settle in the land
questions.explanation: The command is described after entering, possessing, and settling in the land the Lord gave them.

easy.question: Who mistreated the people described in the passage?
answers: The Egyptians
The Canaanites
The Philistines
easy.explanation: The passage explicitly says that the Egyptians treated them harshly.

easy.question: To which land did the ancestor go down?
answers: Aram
Egypt
Canaan
easy.explanation: The verse says that he went down into Egypt.

easy.question: What kind of work did the Egyptians impose on the people?
answers: Easy work
Trading work
Hard bondage
easy.explanation: The passage says that the Egyptians laid hard bondage upon the people.

medium.question: What happened after the family lived in Egypt as only a few people?
answers: They became a great, mighty, and numerous nation
They immediately returned to Aram
They stopped growing
medium.explanation: The passage describes the change from a small number to a great, mighty, and populous nation.

medium.question: Why is it emphasized that the ancestors were few at first?
answers: To show that they were wealthy
To emphasize the nation’s great growth
To explain why they left Egypt
medium.explanation: The contrast between a few people and a great nation emphasizes the people’s growth.

medium.question: According to the passage, what happened after the family went down into Egypt?
answers: They immediately became rulers
They stayed there as a small group
They returned to Canaan
medium.explanation: The verse says that the ancestor sojourned in Egypt with only a few people.

challenge.question: Which connection between the two parts of the passage is especially clear?
answers: The people grew greatly, and afterward the Egyptians mistreated and enslaved them
The people grew in Egypt, so the Egyptians freed them
The people remained small, so the Egyptians invited them to celebrate
challenge.explanation: The passage places the people’s growth next to the harsh treatment they received from the Egyptians.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “A Syrian ready to perish was my father” emphasize?
answers: That the ancestor was an Egyptian king
That the ancestor came from Aram and is described as vulnerable and without a settled place
That the ancestor was born in Canaan
challenge.explanation: The phrase presents the family’s beginning as one of wandering, vulnerability, and instability.

challenge.question: What order of events is described in the passage?
answers: Hard labor, descent into Egypt, national growth, and a small beginning
National growth, a small beginning, descent into Egypt, and hard labor
Origin in Aram and descent into Egypt, a small beginning, becoming a great nation, and then oppression
challenge.explanation: The order is origin and descent into Egypt, residence as a small group, growth into a great nation, and finally Egyptian oppression and hard labor.

questions.question: Which connection between the two parts of the passage is especially clear?
answers: The people grew greatly, and afterward the Egyptians mistreated and enslaved them
The people grew in Egypt, so the Egyptians freed them
The people remained small, so the Egyptians invited them to celebrate
questions.explanation: The passage places the people’s growth next to the harsh treatment they received from the Egyptians.

questions.question: What does the phrase “A Syrian ready to perish was my father” emphasize?
answers: That the ancestor was an Egyptian king
That the ancestor came from Aram and is described as vulnerable and without a settled place
That the ancestor was born in Canaan
questions.explanation: The phrase presents the family’s beginning as one of wandering, vulnerability, and instability.

questions.question: What order of events is described in the passage?
answers: Hard labor, descent into Egypt, national growth, and a small beginning
National growth, a small beginning, descent into Egypt, and hard labor
Origin in Aram and descent into Egypt, a small beginning, becoming a great nation, and then oppression
questions.explanation: The order is origin and descent into Egypt, residence as a small group, growth into a great nation, and finally Egyptian oppression and hard labor.

paragraphs.title: The Lord Hears and Brings Israel out of Egypt

easy.question: To whom did the Israelites cry?
answers: To the Lord
To Pharaoh
To Moses
easy.explanation: The passage says, “We cried unto the Lord God of our fathers.”

easy.question: What did the Lord hear?
answers: The Egyptians’ prayer
The voice of the Israelites
Only Moses’ voice
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The Lord heard our voice.”

easy.question: From what place did the Lord bring the Israelites?
answers: Canaan
The wilderness of Sinai
Egypt
easy.explanation: The passage says that the Lord brought them forth out of Egypt.

medium.question: What order of events is described in these verses?
answers: The Israelites cried, the Lord heard and saw, and then He brought them out of Egypt
The Lord brought them out, then they cried, and afterward He saw them
The Israelites saw signs, and then the Lord heard Egypt
medium.explanation: First the Israelites cried, then the Lord heard and saw their suffering, and finally He brought them out of Egypt.

medium.question: What does the phrase “our affliction, and our labour, and our oppression” describe?
answers: Their joy
Their suffering and difficult condition
Their land
medium.explanation: The three expressions describe the Israelites’ suffering and hardship.

medium.question: What is the connection between the Israelites’ cry and their leaving Egypt?
answers: Their cry caused them to escape by themselves
Their cry caused the Egyptians to free them
The Lord heard their cry, saw their suffering, and then brought them out
medium.explanation: The verses connect the people’s cry and the Lord’s response with their deliverance from Egypt.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the phrase “the Lord God of our fathers”?
answers: The Israelites called upon God, who was connected with their ancestors
The Israelites called upon one of Egypt’s kings
The Israelites did not know to whom they were crying
challenge.explanation: The phrase presents the Lord as the God of their fathers and emphasizes the connection between the people and earlier generations.

challenge.question: What does the detailed description of their affliction, labor, and oppression emphasize?
answers: That the people suffered only from a lack of food
That their suffering had several aspects
That the people rejoiced over three events
challenge.explanation: The three expressions describe several dimensions of the Israelites’ distress rather than only one difficulty.

challenge.question: What does the description of a mighty hand, an outstretched arm, signs, and wonders teach about the Exodus?
answers: That it happened without divine intervention
That it was an ordinary journey by the Israelites
That it was a powerful and extraordinary act of deliverance by the Lord
challenge.explanation: These expressions emphasize divine power and extraordinary intervention.

questions.question: What can be understood from the phrase “the Lord God of our fathers”?
answers: The Israelites called upon God, who was connected with their ancestors
The Israelites called upon one of Egypt’s kings
The Israelites did not know to whom they were crying
questions.explanation: The phrase presents the Lord as the God of their fathers and emphasizes the connection between the people and earlier generations.

questions.question: What does the detailed description of their affliction, labor, and oppression emphasize?
answers: That the people suffered only from a lack of food
That their suffering had several aspects
That the people rejoiced over three events
questions.explanation: The three expressions describe several dimensions of the Israelites’ distress rather than only one difficulty.

questions.question: What does the description of a mighty hand, an outstretched arm, signs, and wonders teach about the Exodus?
answers: That it happened without divine intervention
That it was an ordinary journey by the Israelites
That it was a powerful and extraordinary act of deliverance by the Lord
questions.explanation: These expressions emphasize divine power and extraordinary intervention.

paragraphs.title: Entering the Land and Giving Thanks for Its Goodness

easy.question: Who brought the Israelites into the land and gave it to them?
answers: The Lord
The Levites
The strangers
easy.explanation: The passage says that the Lord brought Israel into the land and gave it to them.

easy.question: What did the person bring before the Lord?
answers: Firstfruits from the sanctuary
The first fruit of the land
All his possessions
easy.explanation: The person brings the firstfruits of the land before the Lord.

easy.question: What did the person do after setting the fruit before the Lord?
answers: He ate it
He gave it to a stranger
He worshiped before the Lord
easy.explanation: After setting the fruit before the Lord, the person worships before Him.

medium.question: What is the correct order of the actions described in the verse?
answers: Bring the fruit, set it before the Lord, and worship
Worship, eat the fruit, and bring it
Rejoice, receive the land, and set down fruit
medium.explanation: First the person brings the firstfruits, then sets them before the Lord, and finally worships.

medium.question: Why is the person commanded to rejoice in every good thing?
answers: Because he bought the land himself
Because the Lord gave the good things to him and his household
Because he should rejoice only at harvest time
medium.explanation: The passage connects the person’s joy with the good things the Lord gave him, his household, and others around him.

medium.question: What does the phrase “the firstfruits of the land” refer to?
answers: The first or best produce
The last fruit of the season
Fruit that fell on the ground
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the first part or best produce of the land.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “a land that floweth with milk and honey” express?
answers: A land that is fertile and abundant
A land with no people
A land where honey falls from the sky
challenge.explanation: The phrase pictures a fertile and abundant land, rich in food and goodness.

challenge.question: What can be learned from the fact that the joy includes the Levite and the stranger?
answers: That only they may eat the fruit
That gratitude for good things should be shared with others
That they brought the person into the land
challenge.explanation: The passage extends the joy beyond the person and his household to the Levite and the stranger among them.

challenge.question: What does the wording “which thou, O Lord, hast given me” emphasize about the land’s produce?
answers: That the person does not need to work the land
That the produce belongs only to the Levites
That the person recognizes the good he received as a gift from the Lord
challenge.explanation: The wording attributes the land and its produce to the Lord, making the firstfruits an expression of gratitude.

questions.question: What does the phrase “a land that floweth with milk and honey” express?
answers: A land that is fertile and abundant
A land with no people
A land where honey falls from the sky
questions.explanation: The phrase pictures a fertile and abundant land, rich in food and goodness.

questions.question: What can be learned from the fact that the joy includes the Levite and the stranger?
answers: That only they may eat the fruit
That gratitude for good things should be shared with others
That they brought the person into the land
questions.explanation: The passage extends the joy beyond the person and his household to the Levite and the stranger among them.

questions.question: What does the wording “which thou, O Lord, hast given me” emphasize about the land’s produce?
answers: That the person does not need to work the land
That the produce belongs only to the Levites
That the person recognizes the good he received as a gift from the Lord
questions.explanation: The wording attributes the land and its produce to the Lord, making the firstfruits an expression of gratitude.

paragraphs.title: Tithes and Care for Those in Need

easy.question: To whom were the tithes to be given?
answers: The Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow
Only the king
Only the priests
easy.explanation: The verse says that the tithe is to be given to the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow.

easy.question: Which year is called the year of tithing?
answers: The first year
The third year
The seventh year
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly calls the third year the year of tithing.

easy.question: What do the recipients do with the tithe?
answers: Store it in a warehouse
Bring it to the king
Eat within the gates and be filled
easy.explanation: The verse says that they eat within the gates and are filled.

medium.question: What should be done after finishing the tithing of all the produce?
answers: Give the tithe to the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow
Leave the tithe in the field
Burn the tithe
medium.explanation: After tithing is completed, the verse commands that the tithe be given to those listed.

medium.question: According to the context, what happens when the tithing is completed?
answers: The person begins the harvest
The person finishes setting aside the tithe
The person sells the produce
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to bringing the tithing of all the produce to completion.

medium.question: What is the result of giving the tithe to the people named in the verse?
answers: They go to war
They build a storehouse
They eat and are filled
medium.explanation: The verse connects the giving of the tithe with the result that they eat and are filled.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “all the tithes of thine increase”?
answers: The tithe should be set aside in full
Only a small amount of produce should be given
There is no need to tithe produce
challenge.explanation: The word “all” emphasizes that the command concerns the entire required tithe, not merely a small part.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by calling the third year “the year of tithing”?
answers: That it is a year without a harvest
That this year has a special focus on tithing
That grain may not be eaten that year
challenge.explanation: The title emphasizes the special role of the third year in setting aside the tithe.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the words “that they may eat within thy gates”?
answers: That they must eat in the wilderness
That they must send the food to another land
That they eat within the giver’s community
challenge.explanation: “Within thy gates” refers to the towns or settlements where the community lives.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “all the tithes of thine increase”?
answers: The tithe should be set aside in full
Only a small amount of produce should be given
There is no need to tithe produce
questions.explanation: The word “all” emphasizes that the command concerns the entire required tithe, not merely a small part.

questions.question: What is emphasized by calling the third year “the year of tithing”?
answers: That it is a year without a harvest
That this year has a special focus on tithing
That grain may not be eaten that year
questions.explanation: The title emphasizes the special role of the third year in setting aside the tithe.

questions.question: What can be understood from the words “that they may eat within thy gates”?
answers: That they must eat in the wilderness
That they must send the food to another land
That they eat within the giver’s community
questions.explanation: “Within thy gates” refers to the towns or settlements where the community lives.

paragraphs.title: Confession of Faithful Tithing and a Prayer for Blessing

easy.question: To whom did the person give the holy things from his house?
answers: The Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow
Only the priests
Only the poor
easy.explanation: The verse says that the holy things were given to the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow.

easy.question: What does the person ask the Lord to do in verse 15?
answers: Give him more holy things
Bless Israel and the land
Forget his sins
easy.explanation: He asks the Lord to look down from heaven and bless Israel and the land.

easy.question: What does the person say about obeying the Lord’s commands?
answers: He obeyed only some of them
He still needs to learn them
He did not transgress or forget them
easy.explanation: The person declares, “I have not transgressed thy commandments, neither have I forgotten them.”

medium.question: Why does the person mention giving the holy things to those in need before asking for a blessing?
answers: To show that he obeyed the Lord’s command
To ask to keep the holy things for himself
To say that he does not know the needy
medium.explanation: Giving to the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow shows that he followed the Lord’s command.

medium.question: According to the verse, what does the statement “I have not eaten thereof in my mourning” mean?
answers: He did not eat it while mourning
He did not eat it in the sanctuary
He did not eat it during the harvest
medium.explanation: The person declares that he did not eat the holy things while in mourning.

medium.question: What is the main order of events in these verses?
answers: A request for blessing, giving to the needy, and then keeping the commands
Eating in impurity, confession, and then giving to the poor
A declaration of obedience, a request for blessing, and a description of the land
medium.explanation: First the person declares that he obeyed the commands, then asks for a blessing, and finally describes the good land.

challenge.question: Which precise detail about the use of the holy things appears in verse 14?
answers: The person did not eat them in mourning, use them for an unclean purpose, or give them to the dead
The person ate them only while mourning
The person gave all of them to the dead
challenge.explanation: The verse lists three prohibitions: eating them in mourning, using them in an unclean way, and giving them to the dead.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the request “Look down from thy holy habitation, from heaven”?
answers: The person asks to be removed from the land
The Lord is pictured as looking down from heaven to bless
Heaven is the land given to Israel
challenge.explanation: The request pictures the Lord looking down from His heavenly dwelling in order to bless.

challenge.question: What does “a land that floweth with milk and honey” mean in this context?
answers: The land is made of milk and honey
The land was given only to the fathers, not to Israel
The land is described as fertile, abundant, and good
challenge.explanation: Milk and honey are images of abundance and fertility, so the phrase describes a rich and good land.

questions.question: Which precise detail about the use of the holy things appears in verse 14?
answers: The person did not eat them in mourning, use them for an unclean purpose, or give them to the dead
The person ate them only while mourning
The person gave all of them to the dead
questions.explanation: The verse lists three prohibitions: eating them in mourning, using them in an unclean way, and giving them to the dead.

questions.question: What can be understood from the request “Look down from thy holy habitation, from heaven”?
answers: The person asks to be removed from the land
The Lord is pictured as looking down from heaven to bless
Heaven is the land given to Israel
questions.explanation: The request pictures the Lord looking down from His heavenly dwelling in order to bless.

questions.question: What does “a land that floweth with milk and honey” mean in this context?
answers: The land is made of milk and honey
The land was given only to the fathers, not to Israel
The land is described as fertile, abundant, and good
questions.explanation: Milk and honey are images of abundance and fertility, so the phrase describes a rich and good land.

paragraphs.title: The Lord’s Covenant and His Special People

easy.question: What does the Lord command Israel to do on this day?
answers: Keep and obey the statutes and judgments
Build a new city
Go to war
easy.explanation: Verse 16 commands Israel to keep and obey the statutes and judgments.

easy.question: With what parts of themselves are they to obey the Lord’s commands?
answers: Only with the body
With all their heart and soul
Only with their thoughts
easy.explanation: The verse says they are to obey with all their heart and soul.

easy.question: What are the Israelites called in verse 18?
answers: A warrior people
A foreign people
The Lord’s peculiar people
easy.explanation: The Lord declares that Israel will be His peculiar, or special, people.

medium.question: What do the Israelites accept according to verse 17?
answers: To belong to the Lord, walk in His ways, and keep His commands
To separate themselves from every nation
To choose a new king
medium.explanation: Israel accepts the Lord as their God and promises to walk in His ways, keep His commands, and listen to His voice.

medium.question: What does the phrase “peculiar people” mean in this context?
answers: A weak people
A special and treasured people
A distant people
medium.explanation: The context shows that Israel is a special people belonging to the Lord.

medium.question: What is described as the result of Israel being a people who obey the Lord?
answers: They will no longer need to listen to the Lord
They will leave their land
They will be exalted and holy to the Lord
medium.explanation: Verse 19 says that the Lord will make Israel high above the nations and a holy people to Him.

challenge.question: What does the use of the two covenant expressions about Israel and the Lord show?
answers: The relationship is based on mutual commitment
Only Israel made a commitment
The relationship was meant to last only briefly
challenge.explanation: Israel accepts the Lord as their God, and the Lord accepts them as His special people; both sides affirm the relationship.

challenge.question: What is meant by the phrase “in praise, and in name, and in honour”?
answers: That Israel will be wealthy only
That Israel will have honor and a good reputation
That Israel will live in every land
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes a status of honor, reputation, and glory among the nations.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that Israel’s special status also involves responsibility?
answers: They are called a peculiar people
They will have praise and honor
They are commanded to keep all the Lord’s commandments
challenge.explanation: Their special status is not merely a privilege; it is explicitly connected with obeying all the Lord’s commands.

questions.question: What does the use of the two covenant expressions about Israel and the Lord show?
answers: The relationship is based on mutual commitment
Only Israel made a commitment
The relationship was meant to last only briefly
questions.explanation: Israel accepts the Lord as their God, and the Lord accepts them as His special people; both sides affirm the relationship.

questions.question: What is meant by the phrase “in praise, and in name, and in honour”?
answers: That Israel will be wealthy only
That Israel will have honor and a good reputation
That Israel will live in every land
questions.explanation: The phrase describes a status of honor, reputation, and glory among the nations.

answers: They are called a peculiar people

They are commanded to keep all the Lord’s commandments
questions.explanation: Their special status is not merely a privilege; it is explicitly connected with obeying all the Lord’s commands.
